processing: Finished sencha leaf is blended with a dusting of matcha powder, which clings to the needles and goes into the cup with the infusion.
harvest_season: Depends on the sencha and matcha used; no particular picking defines it.
appearance_dry: Green sencha needles coated in a bright, powdery matcha dust.
appearance_liquor: Opaque, vivid green, clouded by the suspended powder.
appearance_wet: Soft green leaf pieces, typical of sencha, with the powder rinsed off.
taste_profile: Sencha's fresh green taste with extra body and a creamy, savoury edge from the matcha, turning bitter if steeped too long.

brewing.notes: About 80°C and no more than 90 seconds or so; hotter or longer turns bitter. Swirl before pouring, and pour to the last drop as the powder settles.

vintage_note: An everyday blend, sold without vintage or season and usually undated beyond its best-before. Matcha loses its colour and aroma quickly, so buy small and keep it sealed. Judge it by the freshness of the green rather than by a named harvest.
description:
This is the simple blend its name promises: iri means containing, so it is sencha with matcha in it. The powder coats the needles, and because you drink the powder along with the infusion, you get a greener, thicker cup than the leaf alone gives.

The making is just blending: finished sencha and matcha mixed together. The balance and quality of each set the price, and there is no fixed recipe.

Expect a bright, nearly opaque green, fresh sencha flavour and a little extra savoury body. Steep it short, since long steeps tend to turn bitter. Most of the powder is likely to leave with the first pour, so a second steep will be lighter.

Don't confuse it with matcha iri genmaicha, which has toasted rice as well. Look for a clean green colour rather than a dull one, and treat it as a daily tea rather than a showpiece.
history: Little is documented about when or by whom this blend was first sold. Matcha-coated sencha is a modern retail product made and named by merchants, and no single origin or maker is on record.
